result.title: Asymmetry Tunneling Beyond Adaptive Equivariance Relaxation
result.summary: Equivariant neural networks encode prescribed symmetries as powerful inductive biases, yet real-world data may exhibit symmetry-breaking structure that these priors cannot fully capture. Prior work has largely addressed this challenge through model-side equivariance relaxation, seeking an appropriate level of equivariance for the data. This raises a complementary question: must equivariance relaxation be adaptively controlled? To investigate this question, we introduce a residual path alongside a strictly equivariant model and deliberately restrict their interface to examine the transmission of task-relevant structure. Across five benchmarks, we observe both residual collapse and survival despite these restrictions; we call the latter phenomenon asymmetry tunneling. We further characterize this phenomenon through four complementary diagnostics. Our results suggest that adaptive control of equivariance relaxation is not a prerequisite for capturing potential symmetry-breaking structure.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在严格等变模型旁增设一条残差通路并刻意收窄两者接口，考察任务相关结构能否被传递；在五个基准上观察到残差崩溃与「asymmetry tunneling」两类结果，并用四种诊断刻画该现象，据此质疑等变松弛是否必须被自适应控制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「受限接口下辅助通路信息是否真被使用」的崩溃/存活诊断思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容被视觉旁路取代或信息坍缩的问题；但研究对象是几何等变先验而非多模态推理状态，属方法线索层面的借鉴。
